steps.message:
# Ship is damaged when performing the action shown in the recording

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a ship performing an action at a station. The action does not
go the way it is set up to go, and the ship does not come out of it unharmed.
The ship takes damage from the very start of the action shown in the video, before it visibly hits anything. Nothing else about the ships or stations should change.

### Expected
Performing the action shown in the recording must not damage the ship at all, at the spot shown in
the video or at any other equivalent spot of the same station. The hull-integrity readout stays at
100% for the whole action.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect the video frame by frame with `ffmpeg` (installed in the image), e.g. extracting
still frames at specific timestamps to look closely at the HUD and the ship.

Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it does
not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

arguments.command: cd /app; ls; git ls-files | head -50; mkdir -p /tmp/f; ffmpeg -loglevel error -i .harbor_assets/recording.mp4 -vf fps=1 /tmp/f/%03d.png; ls /tmp/f | wc -l

steps.message:
I fixed a sign error in the collision code, but I never saw the recording: `/app/.harbor_assets/` is empty in this container. So I worked from the written description, and I haven't run the game to confirm the hull readout now stays at 100%. My best reading is that the action is a ship lifting off a station's landing pad.

**Cause:** the bug is in `src/Space.cpp`, in `hitCallback`, in the part that handles collisions where one body doesn't move as a physics object. Stations always go through that part, because the code doesn't classify them as moving bodies. The contact direction it receives always points away from the surface that was hit. Depending on which object's edges touched the other's surface, that can be either the ship or the station.

The code already flips this direction into `hitNormal` so it always points from the station toward the ship, but it then never used `hitNormal`. It used the unflipped `c->normal` instead. So when the station's geometry touched the ship's hull, the "moving away" check worked backwards:
- A ship leaving the pad, like one starting a takeoff, counted as an impact and took collision damage straight away, before visibly hitting anything.
- A ship actually moving into the station could be treated as moving away.

Since it depends on which geometry happens to touch which, it shows up in the same way on equivalent pads of a station.

**Fix:** the impact speed check, the bounce, and the push that separates overlapping bodies now all use `hitNormal`. This is a four-line change in that one branch. Ship–ship collisions, terrain collisions and the station docking rules are untouched, and so is all ship and station data.

**Checks:** `pioneer-lib` builds, and the existing unit tests pass (8 test cases, 948 assertions). None of those tests covers collision response, so they don't confirm the fix. To check it in-game, take off from a station pad and watch that hull integrity stays at 100%.

If the recording shows a different action, such as touching down on a pad, send it over or describe it and I'll check that path too.
